Endpoint Status (verified 2026-09-17): OK (200; anonymous SOAP POST returns data)
Notes / Caveats: SOAP endpoint with two methods (historical and current) - the historical method is valuable because it gives real closure history rather than a snapshot. Requires a SOAP client, not plain REST. PROMOTED TO PRIMARY CLOSURE HISTORY SOURCE (VERIFIED 2026-09-17). Publicly documented: listed on OpenDataPhilly and data.gov as 'Street Lane Closures - PGW'; publisher City of Philadelphia; the service self-documents via the ASMX help page at the root and a WSDL at ?wsdl. Two operations: GetEUNDetails and GetEUNHistory(StartDate, EndDate) where both dates are YYYYMMDD INTEGERS. Returns PROJECTNUMBER, ADDRESS, EUNNUMBER, CONSTRUCTIONSTARTTIME, CONSTRUCTIONENDTIME, REASON, STREETCLOSURE, contact fields. TWO CAVEATS: (a) ADDRESS is a string with NO geometry, so a geocoding step is required before any spatial join - see ID 17 for a validation crosswalk; (b) scope is gas-main work only, so the closure feature means 'utility closures', not all lane closures - state this in the attribution write-up. RISK: legacy stack (IIS 10 / ASP.NET 2.0.50727), no SLA or versioning - backfill the full 2009+ history to the raw zone once (~3 MB per quarter, ~200 MB total) and do not depend on live availability.
